title: Sound for a board game trailer
scenario:
You make the sound for a 60-second trailer for a fantasy board game. A narrator speaks over most of it. Your teammate tried four requests, and each one came back wrong. You decide what to change.

Use the exhibit. The game, the prompts and the results are made up for this case. The models, settings and limits are from the vendors' pages in October 2026.
exhibit:
SOUND REQUESTS (made up)

  1. ElevenLabs Music, 60 seconds, for under the narrator:
     "Epic fantasy orchestral score, 90 BPM, in D minor,
      war drums and low brass, heroic mood"
     Result: a choir sings words over the whole track.

  2. Lyria 3.5, a 20-second jingle with the team's own words:
     "Upbeat folk song roll the dice tonight make the drums
      louder gather round the table friends"
     Result: the singer sings "make the drums louder".

  3. ElevenLabs sound effects, to sit under the whole trailer:
     "Busy tavern ambience, crowd murmur, fire crackling"
     duration: 60 seconds

  4. ElevenLabs sound effects, one short sound:
     "Dice rolling on a wooden table"
     prompt influence: low
     Result: every take adds extra sounds, like a bell and voices.

questions.prompt: Request 1: the narrator needs music with no singing. What is the best change?

options.text: Add "instrumental only" to the prompt and keep the rest
options.explanation: Right. ElevenLabs says most music prompts include lyrics by default, and to add "instrumental only" for music without vocals.

options.text: Lower the tempo from 90 BPM to 60 BPM so the choir drops
options.explanation: Tempo sets the speed of the music. It does not turn off vocals, which ElevenLabs says most prompts include by default.

options.text: Remove the key, since a stated key adds a singer to the track
options.explanation: Nothing on the page links a key to vocals. ElevenLabs says to add "instrumental only" for music without vocals.

options.text: Add an empty Lyrics: header so the model has no words to sing
options.explanation: The Lyrics: header is Google's Lyria method for your own words. ElevenLabs' fix for no vocals is "instrumental only".

questions.prompt: Request 2 (Lyria 3.5): which rewrite fits Google's guide?

options.text: Put the whole prompt in capitals so the model reads it as lyrics
options.explanation: Google's guide does not use capitals for lyrics. It says to put them beneath a Lyrics: header.

options.text: Move the jingle to Lyria 3 Clip, which keeps lyrics separate
options.explanation: Lyria 3 Clip always makes 30-second clips. It does not fix lyrics mixed with directions.

options.text: Keep the style apart and put the words under a Lyrics: header
options.explanation: Right. Google says to put your lyrics beneath a Lyrics: header and to separate lyrics from instructions.

options.text: Ask Lyria in a second turn to delete the line it sang by mistake
options.explanation: Google says Lyria music generation is single-turn. Refining a clip with more prompts is not supported.

questions.prompt: Request 3: what is the best way to get 60 seconds of tavern sound?

options.text: Keep 60 seconds and set prompt influence to high so it fits
options.explanation: Prompt influence changes how literal the result is, not the length. The range is 0.1 to 30 seconds.

options.text: Make 30 seconds with looping on, then repeat it in the edit
options.explanation: Right. ElevenLabs allows 0.1 to 30 seconds per effect, and looping makes sound that repeats without a clear start or end.

options.text: Write "60 seconds long" in the prompt and leave duration empty
options.explanation: The maximum is 30 seconds per generation, whatever the prompt says.

options.text: Make it a one-shot so the model is free to choose a longer time
options.explanation: A one-shot is a single, non-repeating sound. The maximum is still 30 seconds per generation.

questions.prompt: Request 4: the dice need to sound like dice and nothing else. What do you change?

options.text: Set the duration to 30 seconds so the model has more room
options.explanation: A longer duration does not make the result more literal. Prompt influence controls that.

options.text: Turn on looping so the extra sounds play less often
options.explanation: Looping is for sound that repeats without a start or end. It does not remove added variations.

options.text: Add "100 BPM" to the prompt so the rolling keeps a steady beat
options.explanation: BPM sets the speed of music. It does not stop extra sounds; those come from a low prompt influence.

options.text: Set prompt influence to high for a more literal result
options.explanation: Right. ElevenLabs says high prompt influence gives a more literal reading, and low adds creative variations.
